name: Sancerre

rules.yield_base: 65 hl/ha for white, 63 for rosé, 59 for red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

keyfacts: Sancerre is an AOC in the eastern Loire, best known for white wine from Sauvignon Blanc, with red and rosé made from Pinot Noir.
White Sancerre was one of the original AOCs awarded in 1936, and the same area was designated for red wines in 1959.

blurb.text: A Loire Valley appellation in the eastern Loire, highly regarded for white wine from Sauvignon Blanc. Red and rosé are also made from Pinot Noir. White Sancerre was one of the original AOCs of 1936.
